svg.title: Age, circuit dependence, and retrieved content are separate variables
svg.desc: Three theoretical schematics compare changes in memory support and content. In A, cortical and hippocampal representations participate from learning onward. Interleaved reinstatement increases cortical support, with a proposed later cortical readout and a note that retained event context depends on reinstatement content. In B, reactivation adds related hippocampal trace symbols linked to overlapping cortical features; detailed retrieval retains distributed hippocampal–cortical support. In C, an encounter contributes to coexisting context-rich and generalized representations, which support detailed recollection or use of gist under different retrieval demands. The diagrams are qualitative proposals, not measured memory trajectories.

g.text: Original CLS: one mechanism for systems consolidation
Retained event context depends on what is reinstated.
Different representations can coexist and answer different questions.
Related theoretical accounts; schematic proposals, not observed memory trajectories.
